objective.text: Recognize the integer-to-float admission rule even at a strict scalar call boundary.

difficulty.rationale: Apply the permitted numeric widening exception without treating strict typing as exact get_debug_type identity.

runtime.sapi: CLI unless the stated context specifies otherwise
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; no custom handler unless explicitly shown. 64-bit PHP; UTC; C locale.

assumptions: Run in a fresh PHP process using only the displayed files and inputs.

files.source:
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

function asFloat(float $value): array
{
    return [get_debug_type($value), $value];
}

echo json_encode(asFloat(3), JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION);

questions.stem: What JSON does this strict PHP file print? JSON_PRESERVE_ZERO_FRACTION keeps the returned float’s fractional marker visible.

options.rationale: The accepted argument is represented as a float inside the float-typed parameter.
options.misconception: Assuming the permitted argument keeps its original integer runtime type.

options.rationale: Strict scalar calls still permit an integer for a float parameter, converting it to a float.

options.text: An uncaught TypeError with no JSON output
options.rationale: An int argument is the documented exception to exact scalar-type matching for a float parameter.
options.misconception: Assuming strict_types rejects every difference between int and float.

options.rationale: No string conversion is involved in satisfying the float parameter.
options.misconception: Confusing numeric widening with formatting a number as text.

explanation.summary: Strict typing rejects many scalar coercions, but an integer can satisfy a float parameter. The callee observes a float, and the explicit JSON flag preserves its .0 spelling.
explanation.trace: The call supplies integer 3. The float parameter contains 3.0, so get_debug_type reports float and the encoded pair retains a numeric float.

objective.text: Review an attempt to instantiate an abstract base class merely because it contains a concrete helper.

difficulty.rationale: Distinguish shared concrete methods from a class’s abstract instantiation restriction.

runtime.sapi: CLI unless the stated context specifies otherwise
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; no custom handler unless explicitly shown. 64-bit PHP; UTC; C locale.

assumptions: Run in a fresh PHP process using only the displayed files and inputs.

files.source:
<?php

abstract class LabelBase
{
    public function label(): string
    {
        return 'shared';
    }
}

class ConcreteLabel extends LabelBase
{
}

try {
    $label = new LabelBase();
    echo $label->label();
} catch (Error $error) {
    echo 'abstract';
}

questions.stem: A reviewer claims new LabelBase is valid because label already has a body. Which assessment is correct?

options.text: The concrete method body makes the base directly instantiable.
options.rationale: The abstract modifier prohibits direct instantiation even if every method has a body.
options.misconception: Treating abstract as only a marker for missing method bodies.

options.text: The subclass must redeclare label before it can be instantiated.
options.rationale: A concrete subclass inherits the already implemented method without redeclaration.
options.misconception: Assuming inherited implementation cannot satisfy a concrete subclass.

options.text: An abstract base’s concrete methods cannot be called on subclass instances.
options.rationale: Concrete inherited methods are usable on concrete subclass instances.
options.misconception: Confusing abstract class instantiation with inherited method availability.

options.text: Instantiate ConcreteLabel; it inherits label while the abstract base cannot be instantiated.
options.rationale: The concrete subclass is instantiable and reuses the base’s implemented method.

explanation.summary: Abstract is a class-level restriction on direct instantiation. A concrete method can provide shared behavior to concrete subclasses without making the base itself instantiable.
explanation.trace: The displayed attempt is caught and prints abstract. Constructing ConcreteLabel instead prints shared.

validation.keyEvidence: The concrete subclass inherits and runs label.

objective.text: Review a CSV reader that conflates a physical blank line with end-of-stream.

difficulty.rationale: Distinguish fgetcsv’s blank-record representation from its false exhaustion sentinel.

runtime.sapi: CLI unless the stated context specifies otherwise
runtime.errorPolicy: E_ALL; no custom handler unless explicitly shown. 64-bit PHP; UTC; C locale.

assumptions: Run in a fresh PHP process using only the displayed files and inputs.
The fixture contains a blank physical line followed by one CSV record. Blank records must be skipped, while later records must still be read. The proprietary escape parameter is explicitly empty.

files.source:
<?php

$stream = fopen('php://memory', 'w+');
fwrite($stream, "\nAda,7\n");
rewind($stream);

$first = fgetcsv($stream, 0, ',', '"', '');
$second = fgetcsv($stream, 0, ',', '"', '');
$third = fgetcsv($stream, 0, ',', '"', '');
fclose($stream);
echo json_encode([$first, $second, $third]);

questions.stem: A proposed loop stops when a parsed row equals [null]. Which review is correct?

options.text: [null] means EOF, so stopping there is correct.
options.rationale: A physical blank line produces [null] while later input can still exist.
options.misconception: Equating a blank parsed record with exhausted input.

options.text: [null] indicates malformed CSV that must throw before any later record.
options.rationale: PHP reports a blank line as a valid special record representation, not an exception.
options.misconception: Treating blank physical input as a syntax failure.

options.text: Skip [null] and continue; stop only when fgetcsv returns false.
options.rationale: The blank line and EOF have distinct representations, preserving the following Ada record.

options.text: false is a CSV row containing one empty field and must be retained.
options.rationale: false is the failure/exhaustion sentinel, not an array representing a parsed row.
options.misconception: Confusing a sentinel with field data.

explanation.summary: fgetcsv represents a blank physical line as an array containing one null field. It returns false at exhaustion, so a reader must not terminate at the blank record.
explanation.trace: The three reads return [null], then [Ada,7], then false. Skipping the first still permits processing the second.

validation.keyEvidence: A valid row follows the blank-line result.

counterexamples.false-is-empty-field: EOF is not an array record.
